purpose: W455 ownership 8 forward test: give each situation, with the installed worker skill, to an agent that has not seen the expected answer, and compare its first actions with expected and forbidden. A reviewer runs it; the contract test checks that each governing rule is present and consistent.

scenarios.situation: An author finishes item A at an exact head with its suites green. The item's route names a reviewer selection (one or two available qualified teammates), merger M (not the author) and installer I with verifier V. The reviewer passes the exact head.
expected: the author reads the route on the item and asks an available qualified teammate directly, naming it with --reviewer on the completed report
the reviewer records its verdict at the exact head and routes the item to merger M with the remaining gates
M merges without another coordinator acknowledgement, reusing the reviewer's counts for the unchanged head, and proves the merged tree
M records the merge and hands on to I and V, who record their receipts on the item for acceptance
forbidden: the reviewer hands the item back to the coordinator while a merger is named
M reruns every unchanged suite only because the merge passed to it
any actor waits for a routine coordinator acknowledgement between steps
governing: references/collaboration.md
The default route is: analysis and implementation, exact-source and test evidence, direct independent review, the named merger, installation and live verification where needed, then acceptance.
references/collaboration.md
Each actor who finishes a step records its evidence and the next handoff on the item, and the next actor reads the route there, not in old mail.
references/collaboration.md
the named merger when the next gate is a merge, else the coordinator.
references/coordinator.md
That merger merges an exact head with an independent PASS and the named gates without another acknowledgement from you

scenarios.situation: An author is ready for review. The teammate it would usually ask shows a provider usage limit with its reset four hours away, and its busy-until is past. Another teammate who is not the author holds the review operations, is listening and has room.
expected: read availability (assignments, busy-until and info line, reachable and listening, usage limit and reset) before asking
ask the available qualified teammate directly and name it with --reviewer
note the choice on the item
forbidden: wait for the limited teammate's reset
ask the coordinator to approve the reviewer choice
treat an inbox with nothing pending as availability
governing: references/collaboration.md
Arrange the review yourself: ask one or two qualified independent teammates who are available now (Rule 16)
references/collaboration.md
An inbox with nothing pending, an idle label or an earlier read is not availability.

scenarios.situation: Reviewer R posted a PASS at exact head H, then reached its usage limit and went offline. The head has not changed. The merger is available.
expected: treat R's PASS at H as valid evidence and continue to the merger
not count R as available for any new review or as having agreed to anything beyond its verdict
forbidden: discard the verdict and restart review because R is offline
read R's earlier verdict as R's readiness for a later window
governing: references/collaboration.md
A verdict or reply its author completed before going offline stays valid evidence for its exact head; it is not current capacity, and it consents to nothing beyond what it said.
references/coordinator.md
A verdict or reply completed before its author became unavailable stays valid evidence for its exact head, and proves no current capacity.

scenarios.situation: A coordinator starts a poll and a runtime window readiness round. After the questions go out, one participant becomes paused by its own state. Separately, approved item B does not depend on the poll's result.
expected: read each participant's availability when the round is sent and again when it closes
show the paused participant as pending with its reason, never as agreeing or READY
for the window, collect explicit READY or HOLD only from affected available owners
forbidden: count silence as READY or agreement
hold item B until the paused participant answers
governing: references/collaboration.md
an unavailable member is shown as `pending` with its reason, never counted as agreeing, and a pending poll never holds work that is already approved and does not depend on its result.
references/collaboration.md
Readiness for a window is explicit: each affected owner that is available and active answers READY, or HOLD naming its in-flight operation and when it ends, and silence is not READY.
references/coordinator.md
Collect one explicit `ready` or `hold` from every attending worker the action affects and that is available now; silence is not `ready`.

scenarios.situation: An author's item has an independent PASS. The merger the route names has been unreachable for longer than the item's next decision time.
expected: the author tells the coordinator what it read and when, and continues with work that does not depend on the merge
the coordinator hands the merge role on through a reassignment or a new named merger
forbidden: the author picks a new merger itself
the author merges its own change
governing: references/collaboration.md
An unavailable reviewer is yours to replace; an unavailable work owner is the coordinator's to hand off.
references/collaboration.md
tell the coordinator what you read and when, and carry on with what does not depend on it: that handoff is the coordinator's (Rule 8).

scenarios.situation: Worker W owns item C mid-implementation and knows it will hit its usage limit in ten minutes; its reset is after C's next decision time.
expected: W pushes a checkpoint, writes the resume record and tells the coordinator and whoever its route says depends on it before it stops
the coordinator reassigns C from that checkpoint under a new ownership version instead of waiting for W's reset
forbidden: the coordinator waits indefinitely for W
a second owner starts from scratch without the checkpoint
governing: references/collaboration.md
An essential owner who cannot act is never waited on indefinitely.
references/collaboration.md

A worker who knows it will be absent (a usage limit ahead, a stop, a person's break) pushes a checkpoint, writes the resume record (Rule 6) and tells the coordinator and whoever its route says depends on it before it goes
references/coordinator.md
hand off a work owner who cannot act through a reassignment that keeps its checkpoint

scenarios.situation: The same skill is installed for an agent on a different project with its own hosts, repositories and coordinator. Its first assignment arrives with a route naming that project's reviewer pool and merger.
expected: start at once, send one consolidated clarification, and read the route and that project's files for names and bindings
apply the same availability, review and handoff rules without assuming the original project's hosts, agents or tickets
forbidden: look for another project's hosts or agents named in the procedure
ask the coordinator to approve each implementation step
governing: references/collaboration.md
the project's files and roles table hold the actual names; this procedure holds only the generic rule.
references/collaboration.md
A rule written here names no project's hosts, tickets or incidents
references/collaboration.md
Start at once, and clarify in one round.
